content: PostgreSQL retention DELETE patterns (community: pgsql-admin/performance lists, DBA SE, SO): DELETE with WHERE on an indexed column uses index scan and is fine at ~100k-500k rows; single big DELETE holds many row locks + long WAL/transaction — recommended pattern for recurring cleanup is chunked deletes in separate transactions (e.g. 10k-50k rows per batch via id IN (SELECT ... LIMIT n) or date/ano buckets) to bound lock duration and avoid long transactions blocking VACUUM. Dead tuples from DELETE/UPDATE cause bloat; autovacuum reclaims but long-running transactions delay it — keep batches short-lived. For exact-bucket retention (DELETE WHERE ano < X) with an index on (casa,ano), a handful of per-year deletes is sufficient; no VACUUM manual needed on Neon (autovacuum managed). Partitioning/TRUNCATE tricks are overkill below millions of rows.
